title: How Democrats Will Wield Power
gist: FP Live event promo for a Nov. 11, 2026 discussion with Rep. Jason Crow on how a Democratic-controlled House and Senate will challenge Trump's foreign policy; the page also summarizes recent FP Live sessions noting tariffs and the Iran war drove cost-of-living voting, the US buying Russian diesel, and Spain's snap election.

insights.claim: Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate in the Nov. 3, 2026 U.S. midterm elections, giving them power over spending and oversight for Trump's final two years.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Divided government raises odds of congressional constraints on tariffs, war funding and executive foreign-policy actions.
insights.quote: Results are in, and Democrats retook both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 U.S. midterms.
insights.locator: What the Midterms Mean for U.S. Foreign Policy

insights.claim: FP frames foreign policy as an unusually strong midterm driver because tariffs raised everyday prices and the war with Iran sent gas prices soaring.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Cost-of-living politics tied to tariffs and energy creates pressure to roll back tariffs or de-escalate with Iran.
insights.quote: Tariffs have raised the price of everyday goods, and the war with Iran has sent gas prices soaring.
insights.locator: What the Midterms Mean for U.S. Foreign Policy

insights.claim: Rep. Jason Crow, who helped lead Democratic candidate selection across blue, red and swing states, is positioned as a voice on crafting a middle-class-oriented Democratic foreign policy.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
entities: House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence
insights.so_what: Watch Crow and the armed-services/intel committees for oversight actions on Trump defense and war policy.
insights.locator: American voters have given the Democratic Party

insights.claim: Trump's so-called energy cease-fire has not stopped Russia bombing Ukrainian electricity and oil infrastructure nor Ukraine striking Russian refineries, even as the United States begins purchasing Russian diesel.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: US purchases of Russian diesel signal sanctions erosion and tight distillate markets; refinery strikes keep diesel supply risk elevated.
insights.quote: even as the United States begins to purchase Russian diesel

insights.claim: Spain under Pedro Sánchez has clashed with the Trump administration on Iran, Israel, Venezuela and NATO funding, Trump has threatened to cut off trade, and a snap election is set for Nov. 29.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Spanish snap election is a near-term event risk for US–EU trade frictions and Spanish assets.
insights.quote: Trump, for his part, has called Spain a “terrible partner” and threatened to cut off trade.
insights.locator: Why Spain Is Standing Up to Trump

insights.claim: Israel's Oct. 27, 2026 election, its first since Oct. 7, 2023, was a referendum on Netanyahu, with coalition talks between him and centrist Gadi Eisenkot set to shape Gaza, West Bank and US policy.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Coalition outcome affects regional risk premia and Israel–US alignment amid the Iran war.
